newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil prices slip on quiet Euro veg oil market.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil prices slip on quiet Euro veg oil market.

text.p: Nervous liquidation in the Far East triggered a slide in palm oil prices on the European vegetable oil market on Monday morning.
Crude palm oil cif fell up as much as $12.50 a tonne after Nov/Dec traded at $545 a tonne cif.
Traders said the market had started to look vulnerable towards the end of last week as fresh tenders from major buyers failed to materialise.
"The market has been very speculative recently and was pushed too high too fast and eventually the buyers were frightened off," said a trader.

Among refined palm oil RBD oil was $5 down in a tradeless market while olein was $5 to $12.50 lower after material for Oct 10 loading fetched $560 and Nov/Dec $550, $547.50 and $545 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Coconut oil sellers were unchanged to $2.50 up while palmkernel oil was unchanged.
Soft oils were little changed ahead of the Chicago opening with soy oil unchanged to 0.50 guilder down and rape oil unchanged.

"People got excited on Friday because Chicago was up on dry weather forecasts, but there have been reports of rain over the weekend in the Midwest so now they are waiting to see how this is affecting U.S. prices before making a move," said a trader.
